question: Which two 2011 dong-to-dollar conversion rates are shown in Table A.1.2.1, and which is the purchasing-power-parity rate?
answer:
The two 2011 dong-to-dollar conversion rates shown in Table A.1.2.1 are the purchasing-power-parity rate of 7,528.385 Vietnamese dong (to US$1) and the exchange rate of 20,509.75 Vietnamese dong (to US$1). [p069-table-A.1.2.1]

The purchasing-power-parity rate is 7,528.385 Vietnamese dong (to US$1) for households and NPISHs final consumption expenditures (2011, revised). [p069-table-A.1.2.1]

To measure poverty using the World Bank’s global poverty
thresholds, the monetary value of the consumption                                                                          VIETNAMESE

aggregate collected from the VHLSS must be converted                                                                     DONG (TO US$1)

from Vietnamese dong to international dollars. Specifically,      Purchasing power parity (2011, revised)                     7,528.385
the units of measurement for global poverty are 2011PPP           Households and NPISHS final consumption
                                                                  expenditures
international dollars and in per capita per day terms.
                                                                  Exchange rate (2011, period average)                        20,509.75

An important distinction is that conversion to                    Note: The total value of actual and imputed final consumption expenditures
                                                                  incurred by households and NPISHs on individual goods and services. It also
international dollars utilizes purchasing power parity            includes expenditures on individual goods and services sold at prices that are
(PPP) conversions rather than exchange rates. PPP allows          not economically significant.
                                                                  Source: World Bank International Comparison Program, World Development
a country’s income and consumption data to be converted           Indicators.
into globally comparable terms taking into account cost-of-
living comparability across countries. The PPP of currency
of an economy is defined as the number of currency units
required to purchase a basket of goods and services with one
unit of the currency of a reference or base country. The PPP
is computed based on price data collected by countries across
